items.name: Apple Intelligence in China with Alibaba's Qwen
items.summary: Apple confirmed on October 31 that Apple Intelligence will reach mainland China, with testing from November 4 in the latest iOS developer beta and a public launch with iOS 27.3 in December. Alibaba's Qwen model will power selected experiences — Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence — in place of ChatGPT, while the rebuilt Siri AI is not included in this first release.

items.name: Mistral Large 4 open weights
items.summary: Mistral released the weights of Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) on October 29, an improved build after three more weeks of reinforcement learning following its October 6 preview. The roughly 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model is downloadable from Hugging Face under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, with Mistral pitching its coding and defensive-cybersecurity performance for self-hosted use.

items.name: Gnani Prisma v3.0
items.summary: Bengaluru-based Gnani AI launched Prisma v3.0 on October 28, a speech-to-text model trained on Indian telephone audio that covers nine Indian languages plus Indian English in one model and handles mid-sentence code-switching. In Gnani's own Vistaar evaluation it recorded a 16.93 macro word error rate, against 19.98 for ElevenLabs Scribe v2, and it is available now via Gnani's developer API.

items.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on October 26, a fast, efficient model combining detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use with clearer writing. Standard API prices are 50% lower than GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol at $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens, available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex and via the API.

items.name: AWS Infinity agent runtime
items.summary: AWS and UC Berkeley released Infinity on October 23, an open-source agent runtime under Apache 2.0 that suspends an agent when it calls a tool and resumes it from its saved conversation state when the result arrives. In AWS's simulated benchmark about 75,000 idle agents fit in 8 GB of memory at roughly 100 KB each, and suspended agents need no running compute, so the runtime can also deploy on serverless platforms.
